newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Group Five says was too exposed to property.
newsitem.headline: Group Five says was too exposed to property.

text.p: South African construction and building products firm Group Five Ltd said on Friday a belief that its exposure to residential properties was too big was behind its decision this week to downscale the unit in the next two years.
Chief executive officer Mike Lomas said that the property development division had not been making losses, but that it no longer met the group's investment criteria.

"(The downscaling) is the result of a logical decision. The feeling is that we were too exposed. (Residential properties) were too big in our portfolio. What we need is to get a balance, trim it down," Lomas told a press briefing.

He said the division's contribution to group turnover would be cut to 200 million rand for the year to end June 1997, compared with 300 million rand last year, with the cutbacks bolstering the balance sheet.
Group year turnover was seen at 2.4 billion rand.
"We have started the process of downscaling in this financial year. (Property turnover) is less than 10 percent of turnover," Lomas said.
The downscaling would also help Group Five to take advantage of investment opportunities arising in the future.
Lomas said Group Five would honour existing contracts.
Group Five in February reported a rise in half-year earnings per share to 36.0 cents versus 31.1 cents previously. The dividend was lifted to 9.0 cents from 7.0 cents.
The firm said then that all its divisions, bar building and property development, had contributed to profit growth.
